title: Tech Note: Breaking the Rules to Improve Performance, Part 1—Expanding the Concept of a Keywords Subfile
author: Walt Nelson

historical_commentary.text: This note proposes deliberately using subfiles and duplicated ('denormalized') Keyword data to build a fast, forgiving free-text search across many fields with a single index, aimed squarely at reducing painful multi-second-to-multi-minute search round-trips over WAN or dial-up modem links. The core UX idea — a single free-text search box that matches across many underlying fields without the user knowing the schema — remains a genuinely relevant and modern pattern (echoed today in full-text/search-index features), but the specific mechanism (a 4D subfile of parsed keyword tokens, manually built and searched) and its network-latency motivation are tied to 1990s infrastructure and 4D's pre-SQL, pre-ORDA procedural language; 4D subfiles as a data modeling construct have also long fallen out of favor relative to standard related tables.
related_updates: Dial-up/WAN latency motivating this technique is largely irrelevant on modern networks
4D subfiles (a hierarchical, parent-record-only-accessible construct) have been effectively superseded by standard related tables/entity relationships in modern 4D data modeling practice

4D introduced a genuine SQL engine in 4D v11 SQL (~2007), and later ORDA (2018), giving developers standard indexed multi-field search/query capabilities rather than requiring a hand-built keyword subfile workaround
